As the translations are really really bad (being forced to look at German) up to the point that it's hard to understand what they actually mean, the original language should be the default with the option to translate for people that actually need it.

Additional repro-oriented context from the session where this happened:

I had OpenCode Desktop running with `opencode-pty@latest` enabled, and I asked the main agent to do parallel research work by spawning multiple sub-agents/tasks at once.

The parallel branches were doing things like:

- searching GitHub / the web for interactive-terminal-related skills
- comparing `term-cli` vs `interminai`
- checking Windows compatibility and OpenCode fit

So this was not a single serial task; it was a fan-out / parallel-agent workflow from one active desktop session.

The important part is that these spawned branches appear to inherit or otherwise encounter artifacts from the parent conversation/task context. In this run, one branch hit:

```text
ERROR: Cannot read "image.png" (this model does not support image input). Inform the user.
```

My current best guess for reproduction is:

1. Start from an OpenCode Desktop session that already has some richer context/history attached.
2. Ask the main agent to spawn multiple parallel research/analysis tasks.
3. At least one spawned branch ends up with an image attachment/reference (`image.png`) in its effective context.
4. That branch runs on a model that does not support image input.
5. The branch throws the unsupported-image error.
6. Shortly after, the desktop session UI crashes with the `undefined.id` frontend error.

I still cannot prove whether the image reference is explicitly attached, inherited from the parent thread, or reconstructed from session state/history. But the strongest observable sequence was:

parallel agents -> one branch gets `image.png` -> model rejects image input -> desktop session UI crashes.

> I had the same issue and I don't think downgrading the opencode is the good solution. The issue is when you try to generate tasks or milestones or something like this with an enormous amount of tokens in a single response. When the generation process takes too long, the reverse proxy or API gateway handling the Server-Sent Events (SSE) stream terminates the connection due to inactivity or a hard timeout limit.
> 
> SOLUTION : You need to constrain the agent to generate and write the tasks in smaller, manageable batches rather than processing the entire context at once.
> 
> Example of PROMPT to use in this case :
> 
> > The previous attempt timed out because the output was too large. Let's do this in smaller chunks to avoid SSE read timeouts. Reconstruct the detailed tasks for Milestones 1 to 4 ONLY. Write them to tasks.md. Stop immediately after writing these 4 milestones and wait for my confirmation before proceeding to the next batch.
> 
> After finishing this one, go to the next prompt like :
> 
> > Great. Now append the detailed tasks for Milestones 5 to 8 to the same file.
> 
> ...
> 
> Hope it was helpful for you

Seems to be a great temporary fix for now for those that is fine with it!
edit: Also included in my prompt a mini version of this and it seems to have fixed for mine as well

```
Also write the plan in chunks of 3 tasks per writing to avoid SSE read issues.
```

Though for longer plans (10-15+), it might not be a good idea since it will have to generate a lot of extra tokens (though I might be wrong not really sure with how it works in the end), so might not be good for per M token users (non-per-response subs)

Disable editing in ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json. The model will automatically switch to using bash commands, and it no longer hangs. Worked for me so far. ```json "permission": { "bash": { "*": "allow" }, "edit": { "*": "deny" } } ```
